verification.summary: The blocking awk bug is fixed: check_snapshots() now has a BEGIN block setting lastN=-1, so the first marker (n=0) no longer false-fails as nonmonotonic. The stale port-4000 assertion is also gone, PORT now defaults to 4123 matching the contract.

shouldFix.quote: if (n<=lastN) { print "FAIL nonmonotonic " n " after " lastN; bad=1; exit }
shouldFix.problem: Correct now, but there's no test guarding against this exact regression class (uninitialized awk state) recurring silently in future edits — a one-line synthetic self-check before the real run would catch it early instead of relying on manual review.

shouldKnow.problem: This single init line was the entire root cause from the last rejection and is now confirmed present; no other logic in check_snapshots() changed, so the rest of the previously-working dup/cap/truncation checks are unaffected.

application.summary: Most of spec 002 was already implemented; I found and fixed two real implementation bugs that were making the ACCS fail (a stray ANSI escape line corrupting snapshot parsing, and a blank MOCK_GITHUB_URL silently zeroing out the tracker's poll target). `bash specs/002-early-alpha-issues-reader/output/accs.bash` now exits 0, run twice back to back, with `pnpm test`/`lint`/`typecheck` all clean.

picks.decision: how to stop the ANSI clear code corrupting piped snapshot parsing
picks.chose: only emit \x1B[2J\x1B[H when process.stdout.isTTY is true
picks.why: the escape line has no business in a redirected/captured log and the contract's marker-line format has no room for it either

picks.decision: how to print stdout content while satisfying no-console-log lint rule
picks.chose: added a writeLine() helper using process.stdout.write directly instead of console.log
picks.why: repo eslint only allows console.warn/error, and the contract requires these lines on stdout not stderr

findings.problem: accs.bash's check_snapshots awk parser attributes any unrecognized line between two ===SNAPSHOT markers to the earlier snapshot rather than treating it as noise. It works correctly now that the implementation emits nothing extraneous between markers, but it's a sharp edge if a future change ever needs another stdout log line outside of a repaint.
